OCTOBER 2023_PTC COMMISSION MEETING AGENDA
    CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  PARKING AND TRAFFIC COMMISSION (PTC)
  One West Manchester Blvd., Inglewood, CA 90301
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  Wednesday, October 25, 2023 at 7:00 pm

  SEPTEMBER 2023 MEETING MINUTES

A. Roll Call
a. A meeting was held at 7:04 pm in Community Room A located in the City Hall Lobby.
b. Attendees included:
  PTC COMMISSIONERS  STAFF MEMBERS
  Barbara Hibler, Chairperson  Peter Puglese, TE, PE, City Traffic Engineer
  Richard Galindo, District 1  Diana Maximo, Operations Manager
  Kip Rudd, District 2  William Thompson, Traffic Operations Manager
  Brett C.S. Roberts, District 3  Sergeant Patrick Manning, Police Department
  Lois Hale, District 4  Raquel Mendez

B. Approval of Minutes
a. September 2023 Meeting Minutes
 Commissioner Richard Galindo made a motion to accept the meeting notes. Seconded by Commissioner
  Kip Rudd. The five commissioners approved the minutes of the September meeting.

C. Public Comments
 A resident of 117th and Crenshaw Blvd requested immediate attention for vehicle racing occurring at random
  times of the night on Crenshaw Boulevard from 104th Street to 120th Street. Residents are requesting that
  the District 4 Traffic and Parking Commissioner assist with the matter by raising this issue with the mayor
  and council members.
 A resident of 102nd Street inquired information on Residential Sound Insulation Program. According to the
  resident, the manufacturer did provide warranties to the property owner for doors, windows and other
  products used to sound insulate the homes, but the warranties had expired. The resident would like to know
  if the City can help extend the warranty. The Commission recommended the resident to contact the
  Residential Sound Insulation (RSI) Department.

D. Unfinished Business
a. None

E. New Business
a. None

F. Public Hearing
a. To amend the Citywide Parking Permit Program in District 9 at 102nd Street between Century Blvd Local
  Access to 104th Street
 Two residents of the block contacted the Department of Public Works to comment on the request since they
  were unable to attend the meeting. One resident stated that it was beneficial to have the program and the
  other stated that the program is inconvenient and unreasonable, not feasible to implement.
 On the date of the meeting, the following comments were given as to why the resident does or does not
  support the parking program:
   The program must be aimed at visitors, not residents.
   Driveways are not long enough for use and are not part of every house. Currently, residents were having
  difficulty using driveways as the vehicle was blocking the sidewalks and residents had been fined for this.
   Residents are primarily senior citizens and multi-family households.
   Residents have not had any problems with parking during Sofi & Forum events.

  The program is not suitable for the block. The application process is not feasible for all residents due to
  lack of computer access. Additionally, the program does not provide accommodations with driver's
  licenses when the address is different.
 The Parking and Traffic Commission decided to proceed with the voting process. Commissioner Roberts

  proceed with the voting process to end the residential permit parking program.

G. Resolution
a. To terminate the Citywide Parking Permit Program on 5th Avenue from 104th Street to 108th Street within
  District 9
 The resolution was signed by the Chairperson of the Parking and Traffic Commission. The resolution is
  attached to the minutes of this meeting for reference and documentation.

a. None

b. Information on Road Closures and Capital Improvement Project (CIP)
 The information was not available to provide, but the City Traffic Engineer stated that some information will

     PUBLIC RULES OF DECORUM
In compliance with the Ralph M. Brown Act and to further facilitate feedback, public comment is
encouraged at meetings of the City Council, its Authorities, Agencies, and Boards and Commissions, and
Committees and its Agencies, in accordance with the following rules. Please note Members of the
public are encouraged to contact the City Manager, or respective Operating Department Directors, first
before making service requests or service complaints directly to the Council.

    At the beginning of each meeting to consider Closed Session items, public comments are
  permitted to address one (1) or more Closed Session Items scheduled on the Agenda prior to the
  Inglewood City Council convening deliberations in private. Public comments during Closed
  Session shall not exceed a total of one (1) minute in length.

    At the beginning of each meeting to consider Open Session items (Consent Calendar, Warrants
  and Bills, Setting Public Hearings, Departmental Reports, Authority and Agency Items, Council
  Initiatives, etc.), public comments are permitted to address one (1) or more Open Session Items
  (excluding Closed Session Items, and Public Hearings) scheduled on the Agenda. Public
  Comments occurring at the beginning of Open Session shall not exceed a total of three (3)
  minutes in length.

    Public comments are not permitted on any scheduled Closed or Open Agenda item or Public
  Hearing in the event the item has been pulled from the Agenda, postponed or rescheduled for
  another date.

    Public comments to address a Public Hearing scheduled on the Agenda shall not to exceed 1
  minute in length.

    At the conclusion of the City Council meeting prior to adjournment, public comments are
  permitted on any items of interest to the public and within the subject matter jurisdiction of the
  City Council. Public comments occurring at the end of Open Session shall not to exceed one (1)
  minute in length.

    The Mayor, or Presiding Officer of the meeting may, at his or her discretion, restrict or grant
  additional speaker time based on such considerations as Agenda length, volume of speakers,
  complexity of item, or looming threat of loss of quorum.

    The Mayor, or Presiding Officer of the meeting may request that a spokesperson be chosen by
  the group to address the Council when a group of persons wish to comment on the same
  subject matter.

    Speakers are not permitted to cede their time, or any portion thereof, to another speaker.

    The Mayor, or Presiding Officer of the meeting, may invoke the use of speaker cards at any time
  use of such cards is deemed necessary to facilitate the orderly process of permitting public
  comment.
   All public comments are to be directed to the Mayor, or the Presiding Officer, and not to any
  other member of the public or to any single Council, Authority, Agency, Board, Commission, or
  Committee Member unless in response to a question from that Member.

  Any person making a public comment who wishes to provide written or other materials to the
  Mayor and Council must first request permission to approach the dais. If and when permission is
  granted, materials shall be given to the Sergeant At Arms for distribution.

  Commenters must be civil and respectful when addressing the Mayor and Council Members,
  and making reference to others.

  No person attending a public meeting shall engage in disorderly or boisterous
  conduct—including but not limited to applause, whistling, feet stamping, booing or making any
  loud, threatening, profane, abusive, personal, impertinent or slanderous uttering or comments.
  No person is allowed to disturb, disrupt, or otherwise impede the orderly conduct of the
  meeting.

  Members of the audience and speakers shall not wear or display signs, placards, banners, hats,
  costumes or similar items at any time in the Council Chamber that obstruct the view of the
  legislative body or audience members, or which creates sufficient disruption to impede the
  orderly conduct of the meeting or to intimidate other attendees of the meetings.

  Persons making public comment should not routinely expect to receive answers to questions
  posed during their remarks. Unlike Town Hall, Neighborhood Block, and other meetings and
  gatherings more conducive to question and answer format, City Council Meetings are business
  meetings. In many cases staff will be available to take speaker questions and contact
  information and respond in a timely manner.

  ENFORCEMENT OF RULES AND DECORUM
  The Mayor, or Presiding Officer of the Council or Committee, with the assistance of the
  Sergeant-at-Arms or any law enforcement officer, shall be responsible for maintaining the order
  of the meeting and uniformly enforcing the Rules of Decorum.

  In the event that any person breaches the Rules of Decorum, the Mayor, or Presiding Officer,
  shall order the person to cease the offending conduct.

  If any person continues to breach the Rules of Decorum in a manner that disturbs, disrupts or
  otherwise impedes the orderly conduct of the meeting following an order from the Mayor, or
  Presiding Officer, to cease the offending conduct, the Mayor, or Presiding Officer, may order
  that person to leave the meeting.

  If any person refuses to leave the public meeting following an order to do so from the Mayor or
  Presiding Officer, that person may be escorted out of the meeting by any law enforcement
  officer present and may be subject to arrest for violation of the California Penal Code or
  Inglewood Municipal Code.

     CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  Public Works Department
DATE:  October 25, 2023

TO:  Parking and Traffic Commission

FROM:  Peter Puglese PE, TE, City Traffic Engineer

SUBJECT:  Request to Amend Residential Permit Parking District for 3rd Avenue between
  102nd Street and 104th Street within District 9

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the Parking and Traffic Commission conduct a public hearing to do the following:
1. Receive Public Comments regarding the termination of Residential Permit Parking Program for 3rd
  Avenue between 102nd Street and 104th Street within District 9; and
2. Provide direction to the City Engineer on how to proceed

BACKGROUND:
In June 2020, the City Council adopted a Citywide Residential Permit Parking Program. The program is
enforced 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with two-hour parking Monday through Sunday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.
(Ordinance No. 20-09). The program was adopted to protect residential communities more effectively
and efficiently from non-resident vehicle intrusion.

On November 9, 2022, Public Works (PW) Department received a petition requesting the removal of
Residential Permit Parking on 3rd Avenue between 102nd Street and 104th Street within District 9. There
is a count of twenty (20) properties that are within the limit. Sixteen (16) valid signatures (one signature
per residential unit) were submitted on the petition, resulting in eighty percent (80%) of all households on
the block signing the petition in favor of removing the permit parking restrictions. On October 4, 2023, a
notice was sent to all addresses within the petition boundary to attend the October Traffic and Parking
Commission meeting to express their views on the matter.

DISCUSSION:
The Residential Permit Parking District Program encourages residents to use their driveways to park their
vehicles, when available, so that those without driveways can park on the street. Therefore, Public Works
staff requests the Parking and Traffic Commission to provide instructions on how to proceed with the
request by either:
1. Approving the request to start the voting process; or
2. Denying the request to end the processing of the petition.

  Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission
  NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING
  Petition for Termination of Permit Parking in
  Residential Neighborhood
A petition has been submitted to the Inglewood Public Works Department requesting the termination of
residential permit parking within District 9 on 3rd Avenue from 102nd Street to 104th Street.

Per Sections 3-75 to 3-79 of the Inglewood Municipal Code, this matter will be presented to the
Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission at the time and place specified:

  Wednesday October 25, 2023 at 7:00 p.m.
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

This notice is being mailed to all addresses within the subject area. Any interested person may attend
this meeting and speak on this matter.

  Purpose of Public Hearing
The purpose of this public hearing is to give all residents of the subject area listed above an opportunity
to state their opinion of the subject matter.

The purpose of the Residential Permit Parking Program is to assure the availability to residents of some
on-street (curbside) parking spaces within a neighborhood where the patrons and/or employees of a
nearby commercial or industrial facility are otherwise using all available on-street parking spaces.

The Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission will therefore be considering if the availability of on-
street parking is severely impacted and if the termination of a residential permit parking within District
9 on 3rd Avenue from 102nd Street to 104th Street would be warranted. If it is determined to be
warranted, ballots will be mailed to each household within the subject area.

If a Residential Permit Parking District is terminated, all residents and visitors in this neighborhood will
not be restricted from parking on the public streets at any time; including during special events. If you
have any questions regarding this matter, or wish to express an opinion but are unable to attend the
public hearing, please contact the Inglewood Public Works Department at (310) 412-5333.

  AVISO DE AUDIENCIA PÚBLICA
  Petición de Eliminación del Permiso de
  Estacionamiento en la Zona Residencial
Se ha presentado una petición al Departamento de Obras Públicas de Inglewood solicitando la cancelación
del permiso de estacionamiento residencial dentro del Distrito 9 en 3rd Avenue entre 102nd Street y 104th
Street.

De acuerdo con las Secciones 3-75 a 3-79 del Código Municipal de Inglewood, este asunto se presentará
a la Comisión de Estacionamiento y Tráfico de Inglewood a la hora y lugar especificados:

  Miércoles 25 de Octubre de 2023 a las 7:00p.m.
  En la Sala Comunitaria A en el Primer Piso
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

Este aviso se envía por correo a todas las direcciones dentro del área de asunto. Cualquier persona
interesada puede asistir a esta reunión y hablar sobre este tema.

  Propósito de la Audiencia Pública
El propósito de esta audiencia pública es dar a todos los residentes del área mencionada anteriormente la
oportunidad de expresar su opinión sobre el tema.

El propósito del Programa de Permisos de Estacionamiento Residencial es garantizar la disponibilidad para
los residentes de algunos espacios de estacionamiento en la calle (bordillo) dentro de un vecindario donde
los clientes y/o empleados de una instalación comercial o industrial cercana utilizan todos los espacios de
estacionamiento disponibles en la calle. La Comisión de Tráfico y Estacionamiento de Inglewood, por lo
tanto, considerará si la disponibilidad de estacionamiento en la calle se ve gravemente afectada y si se
justificaría la terminación de un permiso de estacionamiento residencial dentro del Distrito 9 en 3rd Avenue
entre 102nd Street y 104th Street. Si se determina que está justificado, las boletas se enviarán por correo
a cada hogar dentro del área en cuestión.

Si se cancela un Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso Residencial, todos los residentes y visitantes de
este vecindario no tendrán restricción de estacionamiento en las calles públicas en ningún momento;
incluso durante eventos especiales. Si tiene alguna pregunta sobre este asunto o desea expresar una
opinión pero no puede asistir a la audiencia pública, comuníquese con el Departamento de Obras Públicas
de Inglewood al (310) 412-5333.
